title: Trump Declares Iran Ceasefire 'Over' as US Strikes Enter 12th Night and Hormuz Tanker Traffic Stalls
excerpt: The president's announcement at a NATO summit in Turkey came as CENTCOM confirmed strikes on more than 80 Iranian targets and oil tankers reversed course in the Red Sea after Houthi threats.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Trump declared the US-Iran ceasefire 'over' at a NATO summit, calling peace talks unproductive.
  • Over 80 Iranian military targets were struck by US forces in consecutive nights of operations.
  • At least 18 US service members have died and 447 have been wounded since February 28.
  • Two oil tankers reversed course in the Red Sea after Houthi threats of a naval blockade.
  • President Trump declared the ceasefire with Iran 'over' during a NATO summit, citing ongoing military strikes and unproductive negotiations.
  • The US has conducted consecutive military strikes against Iran, targeting key military and logistical infrastructure to degrade threats to commercial shipping.
  • At least 18 American troops have been killed since the start of Operation Epic Fury, with 447 reported wounded as of July 21.
  • Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for strikes on American targets in the region, including a data center in Bahrain, though this has not been confirmed.

Ceasefire Collapses at NATO Summit

President Donald Trump declared the ceasefire between the United States and Iran "over" on Wednesday while attending a NATO summit in Turkey. The announcement came after a fresh exchange of military strikes overnight, with Trump describing ongoing negotiations as "a waste of time."

"Iran has repeatedly violated the agreement," Trump said, adding that while peace talks could continue, they were no longer productive. He also threatened additional military measures, including renewing a naval blockade, targeting civilian infrastructure, and seizing control of Kharg Island — the hub through which roughly 90 percent of Iran's oil exports flow.

"Every time Iran kills an American Soldier they will pay for that killing many times over!"

— President Donald Trump, on Truth Social

12 Nights of Strikes and Mounting Casualties

US Central Command confirmed it had "successfully completed" waves of strikes against Iran on consecutive nights this week, targeting military operations centers, maritime capabilities, aircraft hangars, drone storage facilities, and logistics infrastructure. The stated objective remains degrading Tehran's ability to threaten commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

The Pentagon identified Sgt. Angel S. Rampersad, 28, of Ozone Park, New York, as the latest US service member believed killed in Iranian strikes at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan on July 17. His death brings the confirmed toll to at least 18 American troops killed since Operation Epic Fury launched on February 28, with 447 wounded as of July 21, according to the Pentagon.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it had struck American targets in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan, including what it described as Amazon's central data infrastructure in Bahrain, where the tech company operates a regional data centre. Neither Amazon nor US military officials confirmed the claim.

Hormuz and Red Sea: Twin Chokepoints Under Pressure

The military escalation has rattled global energy markets through two of the world's most critical shipping lanes. Iran said two oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz had exploded and been immobilised, while CENTCOM noted that Iran has attacked more than 30 commercial vessels transiting the waterway over the past three months.

A new front opened when Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia on Monday. Two oil tankers carrying Saudi crude to Asia reversed course in the Red Sea after the Houthis threatened to attack any ships loading or discharging Saudi oil, according to Reuters.

Brent crude briefly topped $90 a barrel on the news before settling near $89. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth told a heated congressional hearing that the US has spent $37.5 billion on the Iran war so far. Trump said the Houthis had not yet shut the Bab el-Mandeb strait but warned: "If something like that happens, we take care of it."

What It Means for the Diaspora

India's Middle East oil imports have already plunged 27 percent as the Hormuz crisis forces a shift toward Russian crude. The twin threats to Hormuz and the Red Sea's Bab el-Mandeb could take roughly 7 percent of global oil supply off the market if both chokepoints are disrupted simultaneously, according to Reuters estimates. Higher energy costs feed directly into inflation, affecting everything from grocery bills to remittance purchasing power for diaspora families sending money home.

What's Next

Mediating countries have floated proposals including a possible 10-day ceasefire, though Trump's latest declaration casts doubt on any near-term diplomatic resolution. CENTCOM insists the Strait of Hormuz remains open, noting it has facilitated transit of approximately 900 commercial vessels and 450 million barrels of crude oil since early May. The reimposition of sanctions on Iranian oil sales, announced alongside the latest strikes, adds another layer of economic pressure that could further disrupt global markets.
